{{Short description|Latin phrase meaning "in proportion"}}
{{Italic title}}
'''''Pro rata''''' is an adverb or adjective meaning in equal portions or in proportion.<ref>[http://encyclopedia.farlex.com/pro+rata Farlex's The Free Dictionary] Article is available to subscribers only.</ref> The term is used in many legal and economic contexts. The hyphenated spelling '''''pro-rata''''' for the adjective form is common, as [[English_compound#Hyphenated_compound_modifiers|recommended for adjectives]] by some English-language style guides. In [[American English]], this term has been [[vernacular]]ized as '''''prorated''''' or '''''pro-rated'''''.

==Meanings==
More specifically, ''pro rata'' means:
* In [[proportionality (mathematics)|proportionality]] to some factor that can be exactly [[calculate]]d<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.investorwords.com/5735/pro_rata.html|title=What is Pro Rata? definition and meaning|website=InvestorWords.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Ehrlich |first=Eugene |title=Amo, Amas, Amat and More |page=[https://archive.org/details/greatthinkersofw00ianp/page/233 233] |publication-place=New York |publisher=Harper Row |year=1987 |orig-year=1985 |isbn=0-06-272017-1 |url=https://archive.org/details/greatthinkersofw00ianp/page/233 }}</ref>
* To count based on an amount of [[time]] that has passed out of the total time
* Proportional [[ratio]]<ref name= investigator>[http://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pro-aspirator Investigator web site].  Accessed May 29, 2008.</ref>

Pro rata has a [[Latin]] [[etymology]], from ''[[wikt:pro#Latin|pro]]'', according to, for, or by, and ''[[wikt:rata#Latin|rata]]'', [[Grammatical gender|feminine]] [[ablative]] of calculated (rate or change).<ref>[http://www.thefreedictionary.com/pro+rata The Free Dictionary].  Accessed May 29, 2008.</ref>

==Examples==
When liability for a [[toxic tort]] or a [[product liability|defective product]] concerns many manufacturers, the [[legal liability|liability]] under [[tort law]] is allocated pro rata.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 2006 |title=Manufacturer 2007 Pro Rata Share Responsibility(sic) for Orphan Waste for Maine Household Televisions Computer Monitor Recycling Program |url=http://www.maine.gov/dep/rwm/ewaste/pdf/proratashares2007.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605234527/http://www.maine.gov/dep/rwm/ewaste/pdf/proratashares2007.pdf |archive-date=2011-06-05 |access-date=2016-08-30 |website=Maine.gov |publisher=[[Maine]] Department of Environmental Protection |format=PDF}}</ref> Examples in [[law]] and [[economics]] include the following, noted below:

===Partnership liability===
Each of several [[partnership|partners]] "is liable for [her or his] own share or proportion only, they are said to be bound ''pro rata''. An example ... may be found in the liability of partners; each is liable ... only ''pro rata'' in relation to between themselves."<ref>[http://www.clickdocs.co.uk/glossary/pro-rata.htm ClickDocs UK Legal web site] (quote marks changed to italics for clarity).</ref>

===Bankruptcy law===
When a [[debtor]] files for [[bankruptcy]], and "the debtor is insolvent, [[creditor]]s generally agree to accept a pro rata share of what is owed to them. If the debtor has any remaining funds, the money is divided proportionately among the creditors, according to the amount of the individual debts."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Rata |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/social-sciences-and-law/law/law/pro-rata |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=Encyclopedia.com}}</ref> "A creditor of an insolvent estate is to be paid pro rata with creditors of the same class."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wwlia.org/Pro-Rata.htm|title=WWLIA legal web site|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071006050607/http://www.wwlia.org/Pro-Rata.htm|archive-date=2007-10-06}}</ref>

===Worker's pay and benefits===
A worker's part-time work, [[overtime]] pay, and [[Annual leave]] time are typically calculated on a pro rata basis.<ref>John Steven Niznik, ''Pro Rata'', at [http://jobsearchtech.about.com/od/careereducation/g/pro_rata.htm Job Search Tech web site].</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thesite.org/homelawandmoney/askthesiteqandas/moneyqandas/proratapayment|title=TheSite.org web page about pro-rata payment for part-time work|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070619045037/http://www.thesite.org/homelawandmoney/askthesiteqandas/moneyqandas/proratapayment|archive-date=2007-06-19}}</ref>

Under [[Federal government of the United States|US Federal]] [[regulations]], a [[government]] worker has the right such that: "When an employee's service is interrupted by a non-leave earning period, leave is earned on a pro rata basis for each fractional pay period that occurs within the continuity of employment."<ref>[http://ohrm.os.doc.gov/Leave/DEV01_000063 US Department of Commerce Office of Human Resources Management official web site], citing 5 CFR 630.204.</ref>

The [[American Federation of Teachers]] (AFT), a [[United States|US]] [[labor union]], argues that ''all'' part-time or [[Adjunct professor|adjunct]] instructors should get pro-rata pay for teaching [[college]] courses.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://face.aft.org/index.cfm?action=article&articleID=0c3962ee-cc6a-40d4-bb1a-fe4666b5146c|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070613111711/http://face.aft.org/index.cfm?action=article&articleID=0c3962ee-cc6a-40d4-bb1a-fe4666b5146c|url-status=dead|archive-date=2007-06-13|title=AFT web site}}</ref>  This is an important issue, as of 2010, for part-time [[Teacher|faculty]].<ref>[http://www.cpfa.org/chrisprorata.html California Part-time Faculty Association official web site page regarding pro-rata pay] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930135448/http://www.cpfa.org/chrisprorata.html |date=2007-09-30 }}</ref>

[[Ireland|Irish]] [[secondary school]] teachers are entitled to pro rata pay for part-time work.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asti.ie/faq/prorata.htm|title=Association of Secondary Teachers Ireland official web site page regarding pro-rata pay|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070828211827/http://www.asti.ie/faq/prorata.htm|archive-date=2007-08-28}}</ref>

Under [[United Kingdom|British]] [[employment law]], "Regulations state that, where appropriate, the pro rata principle should be applied to any comparison ... to be given ... holiday."<ref>[http://www.nasuwt.org.uk/Templates/internal.asp?NodeID=68399&ParentNodeID=70003 NASUWT web site] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071009051941/http://www.nasuwt.org.uk/Templates/internal.asp?NodeID=68399&ParentNodeID=70003 |date=2007-10-09 }} ''Holiday'' is used here in the British sense of the American vacation.</ref>

Likewise, in [[Tasmania]], [[Australia]], the law clearly grants workers the privilege of part-time benefits for [[leave of absence]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wst.tas.gov.au/resource/wstfaqlsl.htm|title=Tasmanian Government official web site|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070404144226/http://www.wst.tas.gov.au/resource/wstfaqlsl.htm|archive-date=2007-04-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Long Service Leave Guide|url=http://www.wst.tas.gov.au/attach/longservicel.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060927153914/http://www.wst.tas.gov.au/attach/longservicel.pdf|website=WST.Tas.gov.au|publisher=[[Tasmania]] Department of Justice and Industrial Relations|date=February 2002|archive-date=2006-09-27|access-date=2016-08-30|format=PDF}}</ref>  This is granted under the ''Long Service Leave Act 1976''.<ref>[https://www.thelaw.tas.gov.au/tocview/index.w3p;cond=;doc_id=95%2B%2B1976%2BAT%40EN%2B20070816000000;histon=;prompt=;rec=-1;term= Tasmanian Legislation online official web site]</ref>

===Investment laws===
In [[corporate]]  practice, "a pro-rata dividend means that every shareholder gets an equal proportion for each share he or she owns."<ref name=investopedia>[https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pro-rata.asp Investopedia web site].  Accessed May 29, 2008.</ref>

In [[banking]], "Pro-rating also refers to the practice of applying interest rates to different time frames. If the interest rate was 12% per annum, you could pro-rate this number to be 1% a month (12%/12 months)."<ref name=investopedia />

===Venture capital===
In [[venture capital]], it can refer to the Pro-Rata Participation right and mean "the right to continue to participate in future rounds so that you can maintain your ownership."<ref name=AVC.com>[https://avc.com/2014/03/the-pro-rata-participation-right/ AVC.com web site].  Accessed August 20, 2015.</ref>

===Insurance===
In [[insurance]], ''pro rata'' is used to determine [[risk]] based on the time the [[insurance policy]] is in effect.<ref>[http://www.insurance.za.org/pro-rata-premium.htm InsuranceZA web site]</ref>  It may also be used to describe ''proportional liability'' when more than one person is responsible for a [[:wikt:loss|loss]] or [[accident]].{{cn|date=August 2022}}

===Insurance cancellation method===
Calculation of [[return premium]] of a cancelled [[insurance policy]] is often done using a [[cancellation method]] called ''[[pro rata cancellation|pro rata]]''. First, a [[return premium]] factor is calculated by taking the number of days remaining in the policy period divided by the number of total days of the policy. This factor is then multiplied by the policy premium to arrive at the [[return premium]]. This calculation is referred to as a "wheel calculation".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wheel-calculator.com|title=wheel-calculator.com|website=www.wheel-calculator.com|access-date=2020-05-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106103229/http://www.wheel-calculator.com/|archive-date=2012-11-06|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===College tuition===
When a [[college]] [[student]] withdraws, colleges may refund tuition payments on a pro rata basis.

===Aviation===
In the [[United States]], a private pilot may pay no less than the pro rata share of the total price of the flight when carrying passengers.<ref> [https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/14/61.113 14 CFR § 61.113 (c)]</ref>

===Automobile===
Pro-Ration (pro rata) means if the battery fails anytime within the first two years of service, it is replaced for free. After those first two years, a pro-rated fee is assessed for the replacement. However, the pro-ration (pro rata) is typically calculated from the date the battery was sold.
